authorization: Implementation with separate detailed sprint commits and pushes authorized 2026-09-11; no production deployment implied.
defaultBuildDays: 1-2 focused engineering days; split before exceeding 3

sprints.title: Domain contracts and reference fixtures
sprints.why: New features need one definition of stock, money, identity and reversals before the storage model changes.
sprints.scope: Extract pure sale/tax/quantity calculations behind the existing API; define command IDs, actor/store IDs, timestamps, immutable snapshots and correction links; add independently calculated fixture totals.
sprints.acceptance: A discounted mixed-tax sale, split quantities, loyalty redemption and full void match hand-calculated results; legacy records retain their original semantics.
sprints.exclusions: Framework replacement, database migration and new tax-policy features.
sprints.recovery: Record calculation tables and contract version; compare output to the current implementation; revert the adapter only, without rewriting persisted records.

sprints.title: Awaitable commands and storage boundary
sprints.why: IndexedDB and network acknowledgements are asynchronous; changing storage without changing callers would show false success.
sprints.scope: Introduce one awaitable command/persistence interface using the existing localStorage adapter; route sale, collection, purchase, restock, settings and auth migrations through it; preserve visible behavior.
sprints.acceptance: Delay and reject each mutation: success, receipt, stock display and navigation wait for durable completion; double-click and stale dialogs cannot duplicate work.
sprints.exclusions: IndexedDB cutover and background replication.
sprints.recovery: List every mutation caller and failure path; fall back to the tested adapter only if no newer-schema records were written.

sprints.title: Transactional IndexedDB repository
sprints.why: A command journal and related money/stock effects need one local atomic commit.
sprints.scope: Add a versioned IndexedDB repository, unique operation IDs and atomic command/journal/projection transactions; implement schema-parity reads and writes behind a disabled feature flag.
sprints.acceptance: Real-browser transaction abort, quota, reopen and duplicate-command tests leave either all effects or none; projection rebuild equals committed records.
sprints.exclusions: Real-shop migration, cloud upload and replacing authorization with storage names.
sprints.recovery: Use disposable databases; document the schema and commit boundary; keep production selection on the previous adapter until VERIFY-04.

sprints.title: Legacy migration and recovery cutover
sprints.why: Existing books must survive the new repository and still produce recoverable backups.
sprints.scope: Migrate v2 snapshots to the journalled schema with provenance, explicit opening checkpoints and migration markers; preserve historical facts rather than invent missing movements; update encrypted backup/restore for both schemas; prevent old clients writing after cutover.
sprints.acceptance: Interrupt at every migration stage, resume twice, compare counts/stock/balances, restore onto a fresh profile, and reject an older client without altering either copy.
sprints.exclusions: Deleting the source before verification or reconstructing lost pre-fix history.
sprints.recovery: Publish the forward-recovery and rollback decision table. After new-version transactions exist, reconcile them into recovery; never simply swap to a stale source snapshot.

sprints.title: Resumable drafts and immutable sale records
sprints.why: An interrupted cart should be recoverable while historical receipts must not follow later settings.
sprints.scope: Persist drafts by shop/store/staff/device; version price/quantity selections; finalize through one command; snapshot receipt identity, tax, units, discounts, loyalty and batch cost; define returnable quantities.
sprints.acceptance: Crash before and after checkout, resume a stale-price draft, switch role/store, change shop settings, then reprint: no duplicate bill and no changed historical amount.
sprints.exclusions: Returns, payment verification and cross-device shared drafts.
sprints.recovery: Keep draft and finalized transaction identities distinct; recovery never finalizes a draft automatically.

sprints.title: Opening balances, customer credits and collections
sprints.why: Scalar balances need explainable entries before adding refunds.
sprints.scope: Add explicit dated opening entries, payment-method selection, linked partial collections, advances and owner correction entries; make the customer balance a derived projection.
sprints.acceptance: Opening debt plus cash/UPI collections plus advance reconciles to statements and cash; duplicate collections and cross-store links fail without changes.
sprints.exclusions: Payment gateway integration and silent editing of old balance totals.
sprints.recovery: Carry migrated balances as disclosed opening checkpoints; retain evidence of exceptions; disable new entry UI rather than deleting ledger entries on rollback.

sprints.title: Customer returns and refunds
sprints.why: Voids cannot express partial returns and separate repayment obligations.
sprints.scope: Add sale-linked partial return commands, cumulative return limits, restock versus quarantine disposition, loyalty/tax reversal allocation, store credit and explicitly recorded cash/UPI refund settlement.
sprints.acceptance: Partial return after redemption and partial payment, repeat return, return after price change and refund after shift close preserve stock, tax, liability and cash identities.
sprints.exclusions: Automatic bank refunds and arbitrary negative sales.
sprints.recovery: Use compensating records linked to the original sale; historical legacy allocation uncertainty is visible, never guessed away.

sprints.title: Supplier corrections and credit notes
sprints.why: Purchase edits must not erase cash movements or already consumed stock.
sprints.scope: Add purchase-linked payment history, supplier return/credit notes, correction and cancellation commands; handle paid, unpaid and partly sold purchases with explicit exception rules.
sprints.acceptance: Receive, partially pay, sell part, return remaining goods, settle credit and correct a duplicate: supplier balance, batches, cost and cash reconcile.
sprints.exclusions: Rewriting consumed batches or implementing a general accounting package.
sprints.recovery: Preserve the original purchase and append corrections; block unsupported historical adjustments with a recoverable exception.

sprints.title: Stock adjustments and expiry write-offs
sprints.why: Physical counts and quarantined stock need movements separate from sales.
sprints.scope: Add reason-coded owner adjustments, counted-stock reconciliation and expired/damaged disposal; preserve batch cost and physical/sellable/quarantine distinctions.
sprints.acceptance: Write off an expired batch, adjust undated stock, return a damaged item and recount; totals match the movement log and no sale consumes quarantined units.
sprints.exclusions: Store transfers and automatic financial expense classification.
sprints.recovery: Record actor, reason, batch and prior/new count; reverse by linked adjustment instead of restoring an old database.

sprints.title: Store assignments and stock transfers
sprints.why: Stores need deliberate access boundaries and balanced movements.
sprints.scope: Add staff-to-store assignments and store-specific receipt/target configuration; add owner transfer-out/in records with in-transit stock and idempotent acceptance.
sprints.acceptance: Wrong-store actor is denied; partial acceptance, repeated receipt and interrupted transfer preserve total physical stock; receipts retain their sale-time store identity.
sprints.exclusions: Remote tenant enforcement and automatic offline inter-device transfer settlement.
sprints.recovery: Permissions default closed; migrations preserve existing ownership with an explicit assignment preview; transferred stock cannot be counted twice.

sprints.title: Cash shifts, expenses and closing
sprints.why: Daily reconciliation needs explicit opening cash and non-sale movements.
sprints.scope: Add opening float, cash collection/refund/purchase effects, reason-coded expenses and owner withdrawals; close a shift with counted cash and a recorded variance; corrections remain linked.
sprints.acceptance: Open, sell cash/UPI, collect debt, pay supplier, refund, withdraw and close across midnight; expected cash matches an independent movement sum.
sprints.exclusions: Bank reconciliation, payroll and silently reopening signed-off shifts.
sprints.recovery: Define store timezone and late-entry policy; reopen/correct via an auditable operation rather than rewriting a closed shift.

sprints.title: Statements and reconciliation reports
sprints.why: New workflows are incomplete until their effects can be explained and exported.
sprints.scope: Produce full customer/supplier/stock/cash statements and return-aware tax/profit reports from journal projections; provide an independent reconciliation view and complete exports.
sprints.acceptance: All phase fixtures reconcile across journal, UI, CSV and receipts; rebuild projections from checkpoints plus new movements; test date boundaries and legacy caveats.
sprints.exclusions: Tax-compliance certification and an AI service.
sprints.recovery: Do not mark an unexplained difference as rounding noise; quantify and trace every discrepancy. This sprint ends with a cumulative shop-day verification.

sprints.title: Hindi and accessible core navigation
sprints.why: The primary counter should work without essential English labels or pointer-only controls.
sprints.scope: Complete shell, login, lock, catalogue and checkout messages in English/Hindi; associate labels; provide modal focus handling, keyboard navigation, announcements and large-touch controls.
sprints.acceptance: Complete sign-in, lookup, sale, error correction and lock using keyboard/screen-reader checks; Hindi text, large text and narrow screens remain usable. Exercise actual local sign-up/confirmation/duplicate-name forms, retained existing shop and sign-out/sign-in; label device-only accounts clearly.
sprints.exclusions: New languages and translating the entire money/report workflow in this slice.
sprints.recovery: No framework rewrite; add a visible-string/locale inventory and check missing keys. Native-speaker acceptance is recorded separately from automated checks.

sprints.title: Hindi and accessibility for money and recovery
sprints.why: Secondary workflows carry the highest-risk errors and must be equally understandable.
sprints.scope: Localize new ledger, return, stock, cash, report and encrypted recovery flows; add accessible equivalents for swipe actions, error summaries and confirmation dialogs.
sprints.acceptance: Complete a return, advance, supplier correction, shift close and backup restore in Hindi with keyboard-only alternatives; lock cancels every pending flow.
sprints.exclusions: Regional language rollout and claiming machine translation is native review.
sprints.recovery: Preserve financial meaning across translations; maintain tested key parity and untranslated-string exceptions with owners.

sprints.title: Quantity units and safer noisy-shop voice
sprints.why: Recognizing a number is insufficient if grams, kilos and pack sizes are conflated.
sprints.scope: Add explicit item units/pack metadata, deterministic conversion and alias editing; create a consent-aware evaluation corpus and parser metrics; expose ambiguity/unknown quantities for confirmation.
sprints.acceptance: Examples with 250 g versus 0.25 kg, piece-only products, code-switching, homophones and background noise never silently bill a wrong item or unit; late callbacks after lock are inert.
sprints.exclusions: A custom speech model or a promise of offline browser recognition.
sprints.recovery: Typed fixtures can ship first; actual recorded-audio and target-phone evidence is a separate required gate before an accuracy claim.

sprints.title: 58 mm receipt layouts
sprints.why: A readable screen receipt is not proof that a narrow printed receipt is usable.
sprints.scope: Add measured 58 mm layouts and preview/export fixtures for paise, long names, Hindi glyphs, mixed tax, returns and QR; historical reprints use immutable snapshots.
sprints.acceptance: Rendered width fits printable area; totals match statements; independent QR decode works at proposed sizes; wrapping and page breaks retain all lines.
sprints.exclusions: Claiming a physical printer is supported or adding transport before choosing hardware.
sprints.recovery: Keep existing print/export fallback; publish dimensions and rendered samples, with simulated output clearly labelled.

sprints.title: One tested printer transport
sprints.why: A single proven hardware path is more useful than untested universal support.
sprints.scope: Implement the selected browser/USB/Bluetooth/companion transport for one named printer/device combination; capability detection, permission denial, cancellation and safe reprint; document encoding/raster strategy.
sprints.acceptance: Physical 58 mm print and scan on named hardware; disconnect mid-job; reconnect and explicitly reprint without generating a new sale or automatic duplicate print.
sprints.exclusions: Generic Bluetooth compatibility and broad hardware claims.
sprints.recovery: If hardware is unavailable, push code/report as blocked and keep support disabled; a screenshot or mock cannot close VERIFY-17.

sprints.title: Local pilot and recovery release kit
sprints.why: A trustworthy local release needs real operating evidence before cloud complexity.
sprints.scope: Add privacy-minimal pilot scripts, error/performance capture without customer payloads, versioned release checklist and recovery drills; fix one bounded class of pilot-blocking defects per slice.
sprints.acceptance: Named phone/browser completes a parallel-record shop day, cold offline start, installed-PWA upgrade, encrypted restore and recovery from interrupted writes; compare every money/stock movement.
sprints.exclusions: Deploying to a shop or collecting participant data without the agreed pilot scope.
sprints.recovery: Code completion and field acceptance are separate statuses; missing device/printer/participant evidence keeps the pilot release blocked.

sprints.title: Local backend identity and store authorization
sprints.why: Cloud data must have a trusted identity boundary before any synchronization writes.
sprints.scope: Confirm provider ADR; build local/emulated backend migrations, account identity mapping, shops/stores/memberships and least-privilege allow/deny policies; store secrets only server-side. Integrate provider-backed email/password sign-up, verification, sign-in/out, session renewal and password reset with application forms and a local mail sink; explicit offline-shop linking preserves existing records.
sprints.acceptance: Two unrelated shops and owner/cashier/removed users cannot read or mutate each other's records via direct API calls, views or functions; migration/reset works on disposable backend data. Real browser/provider registration, verification, session and reset journeys; reject duplicate accounts and invalid/expired/reused links without changing the offline book.
sprints.exclusions: Creating paid/live resources or uploading local customer records.
sprints.recovery: Provisional recommendation is Postgres/Supabase, subject to local proof and operating constraints. The current local login is never treated as cloud identity.

sprints.title: Atomic server command processing
sprints.why: Replication must submit validated operations rather than overwrite full shop snapshots.
sprints.scope: Implement server-side atomic command validation and commit for the accepted local command catalogue; idempotency key plus payload fingerprint, authoritative versions, immutable audit events and deterministic responses.
sprints.acceptance: Duplicate retry returns the same result; reused key with changed payload is rejected; forged price/role/store/tax/quantity and transaction abort leave no partial effects; replay cannot duplicate stock or cash.
sprints.exclusions: Client-owned authoritative totals and direct browser writes to protected projections.
sprints.recovery: Maintain golden parity fixtures between local preview and authoritative results. Server audit retention is defined before production use.

sprints.title: Durable outbox and authenticated upload
sprints.why: A lost response must not mean a lost sale or a duplicate upload.
sprints.scope: Write operation payload and local effects atomically to an outbox; upload with retry/backoff, explicit acknowledgements and pending/rejected states; migrate legacy label-only queue entries as non-uploadable evidence.
sprints.acceptance: Crash before send, after server commit and before acknowledgement; reauthenticate and retry; each operation applies once; rejection is retained for review and never labelled synced.
sprints.exclusions: Incoming feed, automatic conflict resolution and rebuilding old queue payloads from guesses.
sprints.recovery: Feature stays on synthetic/test shops until inbound and concurrency gates pass. Rollback pauses transport while retaining every pending operation.

sprints.title: Incoming changes and initial hydration
sprints.why: Uploads alone do not create a usable second device.
sprints.scope: Add cursor-based pulls, paginated consistent bootstrap, ordered/idempotent apply, tombstones and projection refresh without overwriting local pending work; revoke cached access on online membership changes.
sprints.acceptance: Reconnect from stale cursor, replay/out-of-order pages, interrupted bootstrap and remote deletes; no lost pending commands or resurrection; two clients converge after accepted operations.
sprints.exclusions: Silent last-write-wins merging of transactions.
sprints.recovery: Checkpoint cursors only with successful local apply; a second device is not marked ready until bootstrap and authorization checks complete.

sprints.title: Bounded offline stock authority
sprints.why: Two disconnected tills cannot both assume they own the last unit.
sprints.scope: Implement the approved per-device offline stock allocation/authority model, online atomic reservations and device epochs; define privileged online-only operations and observable stock availability.
sprints.acceptance: Two devices race for last stock, exhaust offline allocations, reconnect in both orders, retry after revocation and recover a lost device; no duplicated allocation or unaccounted movement.
sprints.exclusions: Reclaiming unreachable-device stock without reconciliation or trusting a client clock as a security boundary.
sprints.recovery: Default proposal: bounded offline allocations, with no automatic reclaim while a device is unreachable. Until approved and verified, concurrent offline selling remains disabled.

sprints.title: Conflict resolution and existing-shop onboarding
sprints.why: Rejected operations and existing local books need explicit ownership and reconciliation.
sprints.scope: Add owner exception review, corrective commands and resumable local-to-cloud onboarding with counts/checksums/checkpoints; map identities, deduplicate imports and preserve pending work; preview what will upload.
sprints.acceptance: Restore an old backup then reconnect, import the same shop twice, resolve a revoked cashier's pending sale and resume a failed onboarding; no silent rollback or duplicate money.
sprints.exclusions: Automatically selecting a financial winner or erasing rejected commands.
sprints.recovery: Cloud-linked restore must reconcile through commands, never replace cloud history. Abort onboarding by pausing it; retain source and reconciliation evidence.

sprints.title: Cloud operations and two-device pilot
sprints.why: A correct protocol still needs recoverable operations and observable failures.
sprints.scope: Add redacted operational logs, request/operation correlation, health checks, backup/restore runbook, release/migration order and environment separation; conduct a controlled two-device pilot.
sprints.acceptance: Backend outage, credential expiry, schema mismatch, restore drill and delayed acknowledgements produce understandable states; accepted records converge and exception records remain accountable.
sprints.exclusions: Unbounded telemetry, customer payload logs and a production launch without the pilot gate.
sprints.recovery: Provider backup features, costs, region and retention must be verified on the chosen plan. Emulator success is not deployed-environment evidence.

sprints.title: Regional language-pack foundation
sprints.why: Additional languages need formatting, aliases and fallback contracts rather than copied string tables.
sprints.scope: Generalize locale metadata, fonts, formatting and product aliases; translation completeness tooling and fallback; keep canonical IDs/numbers independent of language; scope initially to English/Hindi regression plus pack API.
sprints.acceptance: Changing locale does not change money, IDs, units, sync payloads or receipts; missing keys fall back safely; recognition/TTS support is capability-tested.
sprints.exclusions: Declaring Marathi/Tamil/Bengali complete before reviewed packs exist.
sprints.recovery: Keep packs versioned and independently disableable; translations never change persisted accounting semantics.

sprints.title: Marathi pack and task validation
sprints.why: The first regional pack should prove the reusable workflow with native feedback.
sprints.scope: Add reviewed Marathi UI/errors/receipts/help and product alias fixtures; capability-aware speech/TTS selection; one bounded round of native-speaker corrections.
sprints.acceptance: A Marathi-speaking reviewer completes sale, collection, return, lock, backup and printer tasks; no missing critical strings, wrong quantities or unsupported-speech claims.
sprints.exclusions: Inferring language quality from string-count parity.
sprints.recovery: Use explicit translation provenance and reviewer consent; missing native review leaves the language experimental.

sprints.title: Tamil pack and task validation
sprints.why: Tamil layout and recognition need their own evidence.
sprints.scope: Add reviewed Tamil UI/errors/receipts/help and aliases; verify glyph coverage, wrapping, quantity formatting and speech fallback.
sprints.acceptance: Repeat the shared task set in Tamil, including narrow printer output, long product names and offline fallback; compare canonical results to English/Hindi.
sprints.exclusions: Assuming Marathi validation transfers to another language.
sprints.recovery: Keep the same pack interface and independent enablement; unresolved glyph or meaning defects block this locale only unless shared code changed.

sprints.title: Bengali pack and task validation
sprints.why: Bengali support needs the same financial and recovery guarantees as every other locale.
sprints.scope: Add reviewed Bengali UI/errors/receipts/help and aliases; verify script, numerals, pronunciation ambiguity and unsupported-device behavior.
sprints.acceptance: Complete the shared Bengali task set and then rerun all enabled locales with sales, returns, sync, encrypted restore and printed receipts.
sprints.exclusions: A blanket claim that all regional speech works offline.
sprints.recovery: Cumulative regional release gate: a shared pack-engine change reopens affected Marathi, Tamil, Hindi and English evidence.

sprints.title: Encrypted local vault and key lifecycle prototype
sprints.why: Encrypted exports do not protect a copied locked browser database.
sprints.scope: If stronger at-rest privacy is selected, prototype a versioned encrypted repository, random data key, passphrase wrapping, lock/unlock memory lifetime and explicit recovery/rotation design using standard crypto.
sprints.acceptance: Locked storage dump contains no business plaintext; wrong key, corrupted ciphertext and interrupted rotation fail safely; unlocked limitations and recovery loss are demonstrated.
sprints.exclusions: Claiming protection against a compromised unlocked browser or using a four-digit PIN as the sole encryption secret.
sprints.recovery: Disabled prototype only until independent crypto/design review and VERIFY-31 migration evidence. Do not retrofit encryption by changing one global password parameter.

sprints.title: Vault migration and end-to-end recovery
sprints.why: Encryption is incomplete while plaintext migration or recovery copies remain.
sprints.scope: Implement recoverable conversion of every owned primary/journal/draft/outbox/recovery copy; explicit plaintext-copy retirement after verification; integrate key rotation, backup and cloud-cache lifecycle.
sprints.acceptance: Interrupt every conversion phase, restore and rotate keys, lose credentials, revoke a device and roll forward after new sales; no forgotten owned plaintext copies or lost commands.
sprints.exclusions: Automatic destruction of unowned legacy copies or promising recovery without a retained key.
sprints.recovery: Optional release only after independent review, target-device performance and a documented key-loss/recovery drill; never downgrade new encrypted records into an old plaintext snapshot.
